clue.text: Soldiers madly love sport

indicators.note: acting madly the letters lose their order, so they are rearranged

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, and zero looks like O

explanation.surface: Troops who are wildly keen on games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'madly' tells you to rearrange O (love) with SPORT.
explanation.definitionFit: Troops is a general word for soldiers serving in an army.

clue.text: They're apt, perhaps, to take odd rests at the bar

definitions.text: They're apt, perhaps, to take odd rests at the bar

indicators.note: odd here means strange or irregular, so the letters are set in an unusual order

explanation.surface: Barmen are prone to have unusual breaks while serving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' rearranges APT and RESTS together; the whole clue also describes people serving drinks who idle at the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapsters are bartenders who draw beer, so they spend their time at a bar.

clue.text: Swamp the lower in the upper part, to the maiden's frustration

parts.note: over means above, the upper position
in cricket a maiden over is one with no runs, so a single run spoils it

explanation.surface: A flood sweeps the lower floor upstairs, to the dismay of a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: In this down entry OVER is the upper part and RUN the lower; a maiden over in cricket is six balls with no runs scored, so a run frustrates it.
explanation.definitionFit: To overrun is to swarm over or flood, as an invading army swamps a country.

clue.text: Those who continue the line of show biz types ?

definitions.meaning: people who have children keep a family going
people who finance and manage stage and film shows

explanation.definitionFit: Producers are those who generate offspring, and also those who stage plays and films.

clue.text: The mess she's made about wrong order for lamb

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece is placed around another

parts.note: she's written without its apostrophe

indicators.note: putting the letters in the wrong order means rearranging them

explanation.surface: A woman has botched a lamb dish and left a messy kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong order for' turns LAMB into AMBL, which 'about' places inside SHES, after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A shambles is a scene of total disorder; originally it was a slaughterhouse.

clue.text: Reflective air of overweight hen

parts.note: someone overweight is on the heavy side
a hen is a bird that lays eggs

explanation.surface: A fat chicken has a thoughtful manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Air' is not a manner but the atmosphere: this layer of the ionosphere reflects radio waves; 'heavy side' is respelt as the physicist Oliver Heaviside's name.
explanation.definitionFit: This ionised atmospheric layer bounces radio waves back to Earth.

clue.text: Black or white, with Ian it's wizard

indicators.note: the answer with Ian added gives a wizard, so Ian is taken from it

parts.note: a magician is a wizard

explanation.surface: Ian is a brilliant conjuror of either sort.
explanation.walkthrough: Add IAN to the answer and you get MAGICIAN, a wizard; 'Black or white' are the two kinds of sorcery.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorcery is called black when evil and white when benign.

clue.text: Ten-foot sea-creature, potted for food

parts.note: a decapod crustacean with ten legs, caught in pots and eaten

explanation.surface: A huge monster of the deep is caught and preserved to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ten-foot' suggests great length but means ten feet, i.e. legs; 'potted' refers to the pots used to trap it.
explanation.definitionFit: This crustacean is a decapod with ten legs, trapped in pots and served as seafood.

clue.text: A word amidships may produce cutlasses

indicators.note: amid means in the middle of, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
taken as written

explanation.surface: A word in the middle of the ship might bring out the swords.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amid' puts WORD inside SS, the steamship abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutlasses are short curved swords, once used by sailors.

clue.text: He wants your bloody signature !

parts.note: the devil in the Faust legend gets a pact signed in blood

explanation.surface: Someone is rudely demanding that you sign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloody' looks like an oath but is literal: Faust signs away his soul in his own blood to this devil.
explanation.definitionFit: The devil of the Faust legend makes Faust sign their pact in blood.

clue.text: Father embraces bird-sign of unusual events ?

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold inside your arms, so one piece wraps another

parts.note: Pa is an informal word for father
a hen is a female bird
an omen is a sign of what is to come

explanation.surface: A priest hugs a bird as a portent of strange happenings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embraces' puts HEN and OMEN inside PA.
explanation.definitionFit: Phenomena are remarkable or extraordinary occurrences, the plural of phenomenon.

clue.text: Launcelot in Venetian service

parts.note: Shakespeare's Merchant of Venice has a clown called Launcelot who works as a servant, first to Shylock and then to Bassanio; his surname is wanted

explanation.surface: A knight named Launcelot works for someone in Venice.
explanation.walkthrough: Launcelot suggests the Arthurian knight, but this one is Shakespeare's servant in The Merchant of Venice, Launcelot Gobbo.
explanation.definitionFit: Launcelot Gobbo is the comic servant in the Venetian play by Shakespeare.

clue.text: Estranged lovers, so like successful examinees

definitions.meaning: a couple who have split up say they are finished with each other
candidates who pass an exam are said to have got past it

explanation.definitionFit: A couple who have parted are finished ('we're through'), and students who pass have got through their exams.

clue.text: Stirred up Indiana about name

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: Ind. is the abbreviation for the US state of Indiana
to cite is to name or mention

explanation.surface: A Hoosier is agitated over what someone has been called.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts CITE inside IND.
explanation.definitionFit: To incite people is to rouse or provoke them, so incited means provoked into action.

clue.text: Register the compass

definitions.meaning: a singer's register is the span of notes they can reach
compass can mean extent or scope, as in the compass of a voice

explanation.definitionFit: Both a register and a compass can mean the span of notes a voice covers, its reach or extent.

clue.text: Lures cotton-workers

definitions.meaning: anglers use revolving baits that whirl in the water
people in a mill who twist cotton fibre into thread

explanation.definitionFit: Spinners are revolving fishing baits, and also mill hands who twist fibre into yarn.

clue.text: One loses nothing with knowledge but its lack

indicators.note: to lose something is to give it up, so that letter is removed

parts.note: nothing is zero, written as O
science originally meant knowledge

explanation.surface: Someone who knows things gains nothing from knowing them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses' takes O from ONE to leave NE; 'its lack' is a lack of knowledge.
explanation.definitionFit: Nescience is ignorance, the absence of learning.

clue.text: Selection boards for artists

parts.note: not panels that pick painters, but boards on which painters choose and mix colours

explanation.surface: Committees that choose which artists get in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Selection boards' suggests interview panels; here they are the thin boards a painter holds to choose and mix colours.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter's board for mixing colours is held on the thumb, and also means a range of colours.

clue.text: By the coast in Worcestershire

parts.note: per means by, as in 'per post'
a shore is the coast

explanation.surface: Someone lives at the seaside in a landlocked English county.
explanation.walkthrough: Worcestershire is a landlocked county in the English Midlands, which makes 'By the coast' an odd picture; Pershore is a market town there.
explanation.definitionFit: Pershore is a small market town located in the county of Worcestershire.

clue.text: Results of stage simulations

definitions.meaning: sound and visual tricks used in a theatre production

explanation.definitionFit: Effects are consequences, and in the theatre the simulated sounds and sights are special effects.

clue.text: Be it so — fiat! No end of capital

indicators.note: no end means the final letter is taken away from the word fiat

explanation.surface: A ruler decrees 'so be it' about a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No end of' drops the last letter of FIAT, giving FIA after SO.
explanation.definitionFit: Sofia is the capital city of Bulgaria.

clue.text: Left members of society acting cautiously

definitions.meaning: members of a British socialist society
the Roman general Fabius won by delay, avoiding pitched battles

explanation.definitionFit: Fabians belong to Britain's left-wing Fabian Society, named after Fabius, whose delaying tactics were cautious.

clue.text: Club for the motorist

definitions.meaning: a long-hitting golf club used from the tee
a person at the wheel of a car

explanation.definitionFit: A driver is a golf club for long shots, and also whoever is at the wheel of a car.

clue.text: Disreputable Air Force shark for instance

parts.note: RAF is the Royal Air Force
a shark is an example of a fish

explanation.surface: A shady pilot is something of a predator.
explanation.walkthrough: RAF is Britain's Royal Air Force.
explanation.definitionFit: Raffish means rakish and slightly disreputable in a flashy way.

clue.text: Idly wandering novice makes rustic poem

indicators.note: wandering letters stray from their places, so they are rearranged

parts.note: L is the learner plate for a novice driver

explanation.surface: A beginner lazily rambles and writes a pastoral verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandering' rearranges IDLY to IDYL; L is a learner, from British learner-driver plates.
explanation.definitionFit: An idyll is a short poem describing peaceful country life.

clue.text: Can I be friendly ?

parts.note: am is a form of the verb to be
to be able is to be capable, so 'can' becomes able

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether they could manage to be nice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can I' is rephrased as 'Am I able?', which runs together into one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Amiable means good-natured and pleasant, a synonym for genial.

clue.text: Collaborationist water-supplier

definitions.meaning: the wartime French government that cooperated with Nazi Germany was based at a spa town
that French spa town is famous for its bottled mineral water

explanation.definitionFit: The French town gave its name to the wartime regime that collaborated with Germany, and to a mineral water.

clue.text: It's sound sense that faulty scales can be a trap for the unwary

definitions.text: be a trap for the unwary

indicators.note: sound tells us the phrase works by how it is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: inaccurate scales give a false reading, so they tell untruths about weight

explanation.surface: A sensible remark that broken scales can catch out the careless.
explanation.walkthrough: Faulty scales 'lie in weight'; said out loud this is the phrase for hiding in ambush.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie in wait is to hide ready to ambush someone, so you set a trap for them.

clue.text: The others are, to a smaller extent, fidgety

parts.note: the rest means the others
less means to a smaller degree

explanation.surface: The remaining people are a little less jumpy.
explanation.definitionFit: Restless means unable to keep still, which is what fidgety describes.

clue.text: Brutes resemble the reverse of a saint

parts.note: to be as something is to resemble it

indicators.note: reverse means the letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: Brutes are the very opposite of a holy person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the reverse of' turns ST into TS after BE AS.
explanation.definitionFit: Beasts are animals, and figuratively cruel or savage people, just like brutes.
